scientific_name: Musa spp. (Musa acuminata x Musa balbisiana)
description: Banana is a year-round fruit crop grown under irrigation in Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa, Anantapur, the Godavari districts), Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Gujarat, mostly from tissue-culture plants or suckers. It is a heavy feeder, especially of potassium and nitrogen, and each plant gives one bunch in 11-14 months.
npk_split: Give all phosphorus at planting and split nitrogen and potash into 3-5 equal doses between the 2nd and 7th month after planting (or weekly through drip).

Boron deficiency.name: Boron Deficiency
Boron deficiency.description: Shortage of boron, seen on sandy, leached or calcareous soils and in dry spells. It deforms the newest leaves and, when severe, stops the growing point and spoils bunch filling.
symptoms: Shows on the youngest leaves
Pale white to yellow streaks running across the veins (at right angles to them) on the leaf blade
New leaves narrow, crinkled, thick and brittle, with wavy or incomplete blades
New leaf fails to unroll fully and may stick or tear
In severe cases the heart leaf dies and fingers are poorly filled
Boron deficiency.spread: Not infectious - occurs on light sandy, high-rainfall leached or lime-rich soils and during drought.
Boron deficiency.action: Spray boric acid on the young leaves and apply borax to the soil only as per soil test.

treatment.name: Boric acid foliar spray
treatment.notes: Spray at 3, 5 and 7 months after planting; do not exceed the dose, since excess boron scorches leaf edges.

treatment.name: Borax to soil
treatment.notes: Mix with FYM and spread evenly around the plant; small overdoses are toxic.

Calcium deficiency.name: Calcium Deficiency
Calcium deficiency.description: Shortage of calcium reaching the new leaves, common on acid or sandy soils, after very fast growth or where heavy potash or ammonium is applied. It deforms the youngest leaves and makes fruit peel split.
symptoms: Shows on the youngest leaves
Spike leaf - the new leaf comes out with the blade missing, narrow or deformed
Yellowing between the veins near the leaf edge, later drying into dead patches
Side veins look thick and the leaf is crinkled and brittle
Fruit peel splits at ripening
Calcium deficiency.spread: Not infectious - seen on acid, sandy or sodic soils, with uneven watering and with excess potash, magnesium or ammonium.
Calcium deficiency.action: Spray calcium nitrate on the young leaves and apply lime (acid soil) or gypsum (sodic soil) as per soil test.

treatment.name: Calcium nitrate foliar spray
treatment.notes: Two or three sprays at 10-15 day intervals on the young leaves.

treatment.name: Agricultural lime (acid soil) or gypsum (sodic / high-pH soil)
treatment.notes: Keep irrigation regular; calcium moves into the plant only with water.

Cordana leaf spot.name: Cordana Leaf Spot
Cordana leaf spot.description: A fungal leaf spot of older banana leaves in warm, humid weather, often following Sigatoka or leaf injury. It is usually minor but can dry large areas of the lower leaves in crowded, wet plantations.
symptoms: Large oval or diamond-shaped pale brown spots with clear ring-like zones
Dark brown border with a bright yellow halo
Spots mostly along the leaf edge, merging into long dead strips
Greyish-brown underside of the spot
Mainly on the lower, older leaves
Cordana leaf spot.spread: Spores formed on the underside of spots are carried by wind and rain splash in humid weather.
Cordana leaf spot.action: Cut off and remove badly spotted lower leaves and spray mancozeb with a sticker if spots are moving to the upper leaves.

treatment.name: Remove spotted lower leaves
treatment.notes: Take them out of the field; keep at least 8-10 healthy leaves on the plant and remove extra suckers for airflow.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Add a sticker, since banana leaves are waxy; repeat after 15 days in wet weather.

treatment.name: Propiconazole 25 EC
treatment.notes: Alternate with mancozeb; the same sprays also control Sigatoka.

Iron deficiency.name: Iron Deficiency
Iron deficiency.description: Shortage of available iron, common on calcareous, alkaline or waterlogged soils where iron is locked up. Young leaves turn yellow-white and growth and bunch size are reduced.
symptoms: Shows on the youngest leaves
Whole blade of young leaves turns pale yellow to almost white between the veins
Veins stay green at first, then fade too
Older leaves below remain green
Stunted plant and small bunch if it continues
Iron deficiency.spread: Not infectious - occurs on lime-rich, high-pH or waterlogged soils and with excess phosphate or manganese.
Iron deficiency.action: Spray ferrous sulphate on the young leaves and improve drainage around the plants.

treatment.name: Ferrous sulphate (19% Fe) foliar spray
treatment.notes: Add a sticker; repeat 2-3 times at 10-15 day intervals. Use the lower dose on tender tissue-culture plants.

treatment.name: FYM / compost and drainage
treatment.notes: Organic matter and good drainage keep iron available on calcareous soils.

Magnesium deficiency.name: Magnesium Deficiency
Magnesium deficiency.description: Shortage of magnesium, seen on light acid soils and in old plantations given heavy potash for years. Older leaves yellow early, reducing the green leaf area that fills the bunch.
symptoms: Shows on the older, lower leaves
Broad yellow band between the leaf edge and the midrib, while the strip next to the midrib stays green
Purplish-blue mottling on the leaf stalks
Leaf sheaths pull away from the pseudostem
Young leaves stay green
Magnesium deficiency.spread: Not infectious - occurs on sandy, acid or leached soils and where potash is applied heavily without magnesium.
Magnesium deficiency.action: Spray magnesium sulphate on the leaves and apply magnesium to the soil as per soil test.

treatment.name: Magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt) foliar spray
treatment.notes: Two sprays 15 days apart with a sticker; yellowed old leaves will not regreen fully.

treatment.name: Magnesium sulphate or dolomite (acid soils) to soil
treatment.notes: Keep potash doses in line with the recommendation.

Manganese deficiency.name: Manganese Deficiency
Manganese deficiency.description: Shortage of available manganese, mostly on alkaline or calcareous soils. It causes a typical comb-tooth yellowing on the second to fourth youngest leaves and can blemish fruit.
symptoms: Shows on the 2nd to 4th youngest leaves
Yellowing between the veins that starts at the leaf edge and runs inward along the veins
Veins stay green, giving a comb-tooth pattern
A narrow green edge may remain, later with small dead patches
Midrib area stays green
Manganese deficiency.spread: Not infectious - occurs on high-pH, lime-rich or over-limed soils.
Manganese deficiency.action: Spray manganese sulphate on the leaves.

treatment.name: Manganese sulphate foliar spray
treatment.notes: Add a sticker; repeat after 15 days if new leaves still show the pattern.

Pestalotiopsis leaf spot.name: Pestalotiopsis Leaf Spot
Pestalotiopsis leaf spot.description: A fungal leaf spot caused by a weak fungus that attacks banana leaves already injured by wind, insects or stress. It is usually minor but spreads in warm, wet weather on weak plants.
symptoms: Small brown spots that grow into irregular grey-brown to tan dead patches
Dark brown border, often with a yellow halo
Patches often start from the leaf edge, tip or a wound
Tiny black dots (fungal bodies) scattered in the dead tissue
Dead areas become dry and papery
Pestalotiopsis leaf spot.spread: Spores from dead leaf tissue are spread by rain splash and wind and enter through wounds.
Pestalotiopsis leaf spot.action: Remove and destroy affected leaves and spray mancozeb with a sticker if the spots keep spreading.

treatment.name: Remove affected leaves and dry trash
treatment.notes: Avoid leaf injury and improve airflow by desuckering; feed and water the plants properly.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Add a sticker; repeat after 15 days in wet weather.

treatment.name: Carbendazim 50 WP
treatment.notes: Alternate with mancozeb if the disease continues.

Potassium deficiency.name: Potassium Deficiency
Potassium deficiency.description: The most yield-limiting deficiency in banana, since the crop removes very large amounts of potassium. Older leaves die quickly, leaving too few green leaves to fill the bunch.
symptoms: Shows on the oldest leaves first
Rapid orange-yellow colour starting at the leaf tip and edges
Yellow areas quickly dry and scorch brown
Midrib bends or breaks and the dry leaf tip curls inward
Small bunch with thin, poorly filled fingers
Potassium deficiency.spread: Not infectious - occurs on sandy or leached soils and wherever potash application is low for the yield taken.
Potassium deficiency.action: Apply the due split of muriate of potash around the plant and irrigate.

treatment.name: Muriate of potash (60% K2O) to soil
treatment.dose: as per schedule (300 g K2O per plant in 3-5 splits)
treatment.notes: Apply in a ring 30-45 cm from the plant and irrigate; do not skip the later splits.

treatment.name: Sulphate of potash foliar / bunch spray
treatment.notes: Two sprays on leaves and bunch after the last hand opens improve finger filling.

Sigatoka.name: Sigatoka Leaf Spot
Sigatoka.cause: Pseudocercospora musae, P. eumusae and P. fijiensis (Mycosphaerella leaf spot complex)
Sigatoka.description: The most important leaf disease of banana, destroying green leaf area in warm, rainy or humid weather. Plants reach bunching with too few leaves, so bunches are small and fruit ripens early and unevenly.
symptoms: Small pale yellow or dark streaks running parallel to the leaf veins
Streaks grow into spindle-shaped brown spots with a grey centre and dark border
Yellow halo around the spots
Spots merge and the leaf dries from the edge inward
Few green leaves left at bunch stage
Sigatoka.spread: Spores from spotted and dead leaves are carried by wind and rain splash, fastest in crowded, wet, poorly drained plantations.
Sigatoka.action: Cut off and remove the spotted leaf parts and spray propiconazole with a sticker, alternating with mancozeb at 2-3 week intervals.

treatment.name: Propiconazole 25 EC
treatment.notes: Add sticker or spray oil as per label; cover the younger leaves; do not use more than 2-3 times a season.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Alternate with propiconazole to delay resistance; add a sticker.

treatment.name: De-leafing, desuckering and drainage
treatment.notes: Remove spotted leaf portions every 2-3 weeks and take them out of the field; keep correct spacing and one follower sucker.

Sulphur deficiency.name: Sulphur Deficiency
Sulphur deficiency.description: Shortage of sulphur, seen on sandy, low-organic-matter soils where only sulphur-free fertilisers such as urea, DAP and MOP are used. Young leaves turn pale and the plant and bunch stay small.
symptoms: Shows on the youngest leaves, including the heart leaf
Whole young leaf evenly pale yellow to yellowish-white, veins included
Older leaves stay green (opposite of nitrogen deficiency)
Later, side veins thicken and small dead patches form at the leaf edge
Stunted plant with a small or choked bunch
Sulphur deficiency.spread: Not infectious - occurs on sandy, leached soils low in organic matter and with continuous use of sulphur-free fertilisers.
Sulphur deficiency.action: Switch part of the fertiliser to sulphur-containing sources such as ammonium sulphate, single super phosphate or gypsum.

treatment.name: Ammonium sulphate (24% S) or single super phosphate (11% S) in place of urea / DAP
treatment.notes: Supplies sulphur within the normal nitrogen and phosphorus dose.

treatment.name: Gypsum to soil
treatment.notes: Also supplies calcium; apply with FYM.

Xanthomonas wilt.name: Banana Xanthomonas Wilt
Xanthomonas wilt.description: A deadly bacterial wilt of banana known from East and Central Africa and not confirmed in India, where similar wilting is more likely Panama (Fusarium) wilt or bacterial rhizome rot. It blocks the water vessels, kills the plant and has no cure.
symptoms: Leaves turn yellow, wilt and collapse, starting with any leaf
Yellow bacterial slime oozes from a cut pseudostem within minutes
Fruit ripens early and unevenly, with rusty-brown stains inside the pulp
Male bud and bunch stalk shrivel and blacken
Whole mat dies
Xanthomonas wilt.spread: Spread by cutting tools, insects visiting the male flower, infected suckers and contact with diseased plant sap.
Xanthomonas wilt.action: Stop moving suckers out of the field, uproot and bury the affected plants, disinfect knives between plants and report the case to the horticulture department for confirmation.

treatment.name: Uproot and bury or burn affected mats
treatment.notes: No chemical cures an infected plant; do not replant banana in that spot for at least 6 months.

treatment.name: Disinfect cutting tools between plants
treatment.notes: Flame the blade or dip it in household bleach solution before moving to the next plant.

treatment.name: Break off the male bud with a forked stick after the last hand forms
treatment.notes: Removes the entry point for insect-carried bacteria; do not use a knife.

Zinc deficiency.name: Zinc Deficiency
Zinc deficiency.description: Shortage of available zinc, common on alkaline, calcareous or sandy soils and where phosphate is applied heavily. New leaves stay narrow and striped, and bunches are small with twisted fingers.
symptoms: Shows on the youngest leaves
New leaves narrow, small and lance-shaped
Alternating yellow-white and green stripes between the side veins
Reddish-purple colour on the underside of the unrolling leaf
Leaves crowded at the top; fingers small, twisted and pale at the tip
Zinc deficiency.spread: Not infectious - occurs on high-pH, lime-rich or sandy soils and with heavy phosphate use.
Zinc deficiency.action: Spray zinc sulphate on the young leaves.

treatment.name: Zinc sulphate (21% Zn) foliar spray
treatment.notes: Add a sticker; spray at 3, 5 and 7 months after planting or as soon as symptoms appear.

treatment.name: Zinc sulphate to soil
treatment.notes: Apply with FYM, not mixed with phosphate fertiliser.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease or nutrient deficiency. A broad, evenly green blade indicates a well-fed, well-watered plant.
symptoms: Uniform green leaf blade with no streaks, spots or yellow bands
Leaf edge green and intact apart from normal wind tearing
New leaves unroll fully and are of normal width
healthy.action: Continue the fertiliser splits, regular irrigation, desuckering and removal of old dry leaves.
